title: Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Smoking deaths and social cost
sections.summary: Over 2,000 Singaporeans die prematurely yearly from smoking-related diseases, with social costs estimated at least S$600 million a year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: More than 2,000 Singaporeans die prematurely from smoking-related diseases each year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The social cost of smoking in Singapore has been conservatively estimated to be at least S$600 million a year in direct healthcare costs as well as lost productivity.

sections.label: Falling Singapore smoking rates
sections.summary: Smoking rates in Singapore fell from 23% in 1977 to 19% in 1984 and 12.6% in 2004.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As a result of these efforts, smoking rates in Singapore fell from 23% in 1977 to 19% in 1984, and further to 12.6% in 2004.

sections.label: Australian standardised packaging study
sections.summary: An Australian Government-commissioned study found standardised packaging reduced Australia's smoking prevalence by 0.55 percentage points between December 2012 and September 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: According to a study commissioned by the Australian Government, between December 2012 and September 2015, standardised packaging was responsible for reducing the country's smoking prevalence by 0.55 percentage points.

sections.label: Branded packaging and youth smoking
sections.summary: Branded packaging's role in encouraging children and young adults to smoke is of concern in Singapore, where over 90% of smokers start before age 21.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The role that branded packaging plays in encouraging children and young adults to experiment with tobacco and to establish and continue a habit of smoking is one that is of particular concern in Singapore, where more than 90% of smokers initiate smoking before the age of 21.

sections.label: Standardised packaging public health objectives
sections.summary: The Government assesses that standardised packaging with enlarged graphic health warnings will achieve five public health objectives and justifies clause 3's repeal of sections 17 and 17A.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Ultimately, Mr Speaker, our final assessment of the available international and local evidence is this – that the introduction of standardised packaging in Singapore, taken together with enlarged graphic health warnings, or the "SP Proposal", will be effective in achieving five public health objectives, namely: first, reducing the attractiveness of tobacco products; secondly eliminating the effects of tobacco packaging as a form of advertising and promotion; third, reducing the ability of tobacco packaging to mislead about the harmful effects of smoking; fourth, increasing the noticeability and effectiveness of mandatory GHWs; and finally, better informing smokers and non-smokers of the risks associated with tobacco use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the Government expects that these will lead to positive future public health outcomes, such as reduced smoking prevalence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: It is in light of the foregoing that the Government considers the introduction of standardised packaging together with enlarged graphic health warnings to be justified from a public health perspective.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: First, clause 3 of the Bill repeals the existing sections 17 and 17A of the Act and substitutes a new section 17, which enables the implementation of standardised packaging for tobacco products.

sections.label: Removal of tobacco packaging elements
sections.summary: The first measure includes removing all colours, logos, brand images and promotional information from tobacco retail packaging.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The first will include the removal of all colours, logos, brand images and promotional information on the retail packaging of tobacco products.

sections.label: WTO Panel on Australia packaging
sections.summary: A WTO dispute settlement Panel found Australia's standardised packaging measures were not inconsistent with its WTO obligations, including TRIPS and the TBT Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In this regard, it is also worth noting that a dispute settlement Panel of the World Trade Organization (WTO) has found that Australia's introduction of standardised packaging measures was not inconsistent with its international obligations under various WTO agreements, including the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) and the Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) Agreement.

sections.label: Clause 5 compounding offences
sections.summary: Clause 5 amends section 34 of the Act to allow compoundable offences to be compounded for a sum not exceeding the lower of half the maximum fine or $5,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill amends section 34 of the Act, to allow compoundable offences to be compounded for a sum not exceeding the lower of one half of the amount of the maximum fine prescribed for the offence or $5,000.

sections.label: Clause 4 increased fines
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends section 18 of the Act to raise maximum fines from $5,000 to $10,000 for a first offence and from $10,000 to $20,000 for a person with a previous qualifying conviction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill amends section 18 of the Act, to increase the maximum fines for an offence under that section from $5,000 to $10,000 for a first offence; and from $10,000 to $20,000 for a person who has any previous qualifying conviction.

sections.label: MOH view on SP Proposal
sections.summary: MOH believes the SP Proposal is likely to achieve its public health objectives and contribute to reducing smoking prevalence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Based on our review of the evidence and the feedback, MOH is of the view that there are convincing grounds to believe that the SP Proposal is likely to achieve its public health objectives and, ultimately, is likely to operate alongside other existing and possible future tobacco control measures to contribute towards promoting public health through the reduction of the prevalence of smoking in Singapore and thereby constitute a significant step towards Singapore becoming a tobacco-free society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: When introduced, the SP Proposal will form part of a comprehensive suite of tobacco-control measures in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: It will operate alongside other existing and possible future tobacco-control measures to contribute towards our Government's obligations under the FCTC and towards reducing the prevalence of smoking in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This would constitute a significant step towards Singapore's long-standing public health objective of promoting and moving towards a tobacco-free society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Over the past few years, we have made important strides in curbing the pernicious influence of smoking, through point-of-sale display bans, raising the minimum age for smoking, and restricting public areas where smoking is permitted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The evidence that plain packaging reduces the allure of cigarettes and so reduces smoking initiation and may even improve smoking cessation rates is substantial and convincing.

sections.label: Concerns about plain packaging
sections.summary: Concerns were raised that standard packaging could lead to down trading and could facilitate counterfeiting of cigarettes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, concerns have been raised that standard packaging of cigarettes and tobacco products could lead to the phenomenon of "down trading", where smokers will just switch to cheaper products as it would be harder to distinguish between various products.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, concerns have also been raised that plain packaging could facilitate counterfeiting of cigarettes.

sections.label: Countries with plain packaging
sections.summary: Australia first introduced plain packaging for tobacco in 2011, and several countries have since passed plain packaging legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Australia was the first country to introduce plain packaging requirement for tobacco in 2011 though the idea appears to have originated from New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In recent years, quite a few countries have passed legislation to require plain packaging for tobacco, such as New Zealand, France, the UK, Ireland, Norway, Slovenia, Canada and Uruguay.

sections.label: Tobacco packaging transition questions
sections.summary: An MP asks about tobacco companies' and retailers' transition to new packaging, transition time, and consistency with bringing in foreign cigarettes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In either of these cases, tobacco companies took the opportunity to maximise the publicity of outgoing branding and attempted to desensitise smokers to the change in packaging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to know what are the Government's plans for the tobacco companies' and retailers' transition to the new packaging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There should be a good balance struck between giving tobacco companies sufficient transition time, but not any longer, so that these companies will not have more time to plan their marketing to work around the limitations of the new packaging requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Government whether the new rules on plain packaging will be inconsistent with the current practice of allowing people to bring in cigarettes from foreign countries by declaring and paying tariffs for such cigarettes.

sections.label: Plain packaging by 2020
sections.summary: By 2020, tobacco sold in Singapore must use drab colours, drop logos and promotional information, and carry larger graphic warnings.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By 2020, tobacco sold in Singapore must be packaged in drab colours, dropping logos, brand images and all other promotional information, while the size of the graphic warning is increased.

sections.label: Nee Soon South DSPs
sections.summary: Nee Soon South is covered by 50 DSPs, costing about half a million dollars raised from private donors.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Today, Nee Soon South is covered by 50 DSPs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This cost us about half a million dollars, raised from private donors.

sections.label: Smuggling and heavier penalties
sections.summary: An MP asks how cigarettes were smuggled in and hopes heavier penalties for illegal tobacco import will deter it.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While I applaud these organisations for their diligence, I would like to know how these cigarettes were smuggled in and what is being done about it.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that the proposed amendments include imposing heavier penalties on illegal import of tobacco products, and I hope that this will serve as some form of deterrence.

sections.label: Small shops, fines, DSPs
sections.summary: An MP seeks time for small shops to sell old stock, says fines are insufficient and jail terms would deter more, and asks for more DSPs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can show some understanding towards small provision shops by allowing them sufficient time to sell their old stock.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This amendment will increase the fine on contraband cigarettes.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, successful cigarette-smuggling has big profits in it and, hence, fines are not enough to deter cigarette-smuggling.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we impose jail terms, the deterrent effect will be much stronger.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Although we hope that all can quit smoking, surely there will be some people who cannot kick the habit.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can consider setting up more DSPs to protect others from the harmful effects of second-hand smoking.

sections.label: Smoking prevalence and starting age
sections.summary: Singapore has seen no sustained decline in smoking prevalence, hovering between 12% and 14%, and 80% of adult smokers started before 21.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, Singapore has seen no definitive patterns of sustained decline in smoking prevalence, which has hovered between 12% and 14%.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notably, research by the Singapore Cancer Society found that 80% of adult smokers in Singapore picked up the habit before reaching 21.

sections.label: Tobacco social media hashtag views
sections.summary: Petitioners' research found 123 tobacco-linked hashtags viewed 8.8 billion times in the US and 25 billion times worldwide on Twitter.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Research by the petitioners found that a mere 123 hashtags linked to these tobacco companies’ social media campaigns were viewed 8.8 billion times in the US and 25 billion times worldwide just on Twitter alone.

sections.label: Requests on tobacco social media promotion
sections.summary: The speaker asks about tracking tobacco and e-cigarette social media promotion, guidelines for influencers, ASEAN and WHO action, and engaging technology companies.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such transnational social media campaigns that actively promote smoking will undo the value and hard work of anti-tobacco legislation and enforcement that have been in place worldwide for decades.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether there will be greater effort made to track the use of social media by tobacco and e-cigarette companies for promoting their wares in Singapore through such underhanded methods.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask whether the Ministry will work with the Advertising Standards Authority of Singapore to establish more concrete guidelines around the responsibilities of social media influencers with regard to full disclosure in cases of sponsored content by tobacco and e-cigarette companies.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would further like to suggest that the Ministry work with its counterparts in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and countries further afield, as well as WHO, to take action against this egregious and damaging practice of using social media campaigns to circumvent restrictions against tobacco advertisements.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, I would also like to suggest that the Minister engage with big technology companies to remind them of the contributory and supportive role they should play in helping to minimise young people’s exposure to images portraying smoking in a positive light.

sections.label: Concerns on covert smoking promotion
sections.summary: The speaker registers concerns about novel and surreptitious ways of promoting smoking and vaping, supports the Bill, and hopes for monitoring of covert marketing.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): In conclusion, Mr Speaker, I hereby register my concerns about the deleterious trends surrounding novel and surreptitious ways of promoting smoking and vaping.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I strongly support this Bill and hope that the Ministry will monitor such covert marketing to Singapore’s youths, with a view to an even stronger Bill in future.

sections.label: IMH study on smoking addiction
sections.summary: A 2010 Institute of Mental Health study showed 4.5% of Singaporeans are addicted to smoking and 20% of them are Malays.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: A study by the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) in 2010 showed that 4.5% of Singaporeans are addicted to smoking and 20% of them are Malays, which represents a higher proportion compared to our population figures as a minority group.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Programmes like the I QUIT Programme/Challenge to Quit Smoking during the Fasting Month of Ramadan, advertisements and others, as well as various measures by the Government, seem to have lost their effect.

sections.label: Commending MOH initiatives and literature
sections.summary: The speaker commends MOH's initiatives over the years and notes literature from several countries showing implementation was lukewarm and controversial.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We have had all kinds of efforts put in and I have to commend MOH for all the initiatives that have been undertaken over the years.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We have seen the literature from several countries and have seen how this implementation has been rather lukewarm and, in fact, controversial in some countries.

sections.label: Clause 4 increases fines
sections.summary: Clause 4 of the Bill amends section 18(5) of the Act to increase fines for an offence under that provision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill amends section 18(5) of the Act to increase the fines for an offence under that provision.

sections.label: Fines increased for offenders
sections.summary: The passage asks why fines have been increased by 100% for both offenders and repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Further, why have these fines been increased by 100%, both in the case of offenders and repeat offenders?

sections.label: Australia tobacco packaging enforcement committee
sections.summary: Australia, first to introduce standardised packaging, set up a Tobacco Plain Packaging Enforcement Committee with Health Ministry and National Measurement Institute representatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Australia, the first country to introduce standardised packaging, set up a Tobacco Plain Packaging Enforcement Committee comprising representatives from the Ministry of Health and the National Measurement Institute.

sections.label: Standardised packaging reduces smoking appeal
sections.summary: Research projects found such packaging helps reduce tobacco products' appeal and seems effective in reducing smoking where introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As various research projects have found, such packaging will help to reduce the appeal of tobacco products and seems effective in reducing smoking in countries when standardised packaging was introduced.

sections.label: Hard ban on tobacco imports rejected
sections.summary: The Government concluded a hard ban on tobacco imports is inadvisable as it would drive buying and selling underground and encourage smuggling, so products remain on shelves without customised designs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some of my residents have asked me if the Government would consider banning the import of tobacco products altogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We had discussed this option in this House before and concluded that a hard ban would not be advisable as this would just drive the buying and selling underground, and encourage smuggling, particularly from across the Causeway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is better, for now, to allow tobacco products to remain on the shelves of our shops and supermarkets while removing the customised designs of each brand and product.

sections.label: Bill addresses smoking prevalence decline
sections.summary: The Bill recognises more must be done for sustained declines in smoking prevalence, with one in five men smoking daily, higher than many developed countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At its heart, this Bill recognises that more needs to be done to achieve the sustained declines in smoking prevalence, and I reiterate the statistic that I mentioned at the start of this session, which is, that one in five men smoke daily, higher than in many developed countries.

sections.label: MOH review of packaging studies
sections.summary: MOH reviewed over 200 primary studies, reviews and materials on standardised packaging and enlarged GHWs from many sources, countries and disciplines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: MOH has reviewed over 200 primary studies, reviews and materials relating to standardised packaging and enlarged GHWs originating from a wide range of sources and countries, and also across multiple disciplines, such as public health, marketing, psychology, economics and econometrics.

sections.label: Quitline calls rise
sections.summary: Quitline calls rose 78%, peaking at four weeks and sustained through 43 weeks post-implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The number of calls to Quitline also rose by 78%, peaking at four weeks post-implementation, and sustained right through 43 weeks post-implementation.

sections.label: Australia results applied to Singapore
sections.summary: Applying Australia's results at the same rate in Singapore would mean 15,000 fewer smokers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To put the results that they have achieved in context, if you were to apply that in Singapore, at the same rate that they have achieved in Australia, it would mean a reduction of 15,000 fewer smokers here.

sections.label: Review of graphic health warnings
sections.summary: A review of 32 studies from 20 countries found GHWs associated with increased Quitline calls and reduced smoking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For example, a systematic review of 32 studies from 20 countries, including some high-income countries, with more than 800,000 participants found that GHWs are associated with increased Quitline calls, reduced smoking consumption, increased quit attempts, increased short-term smoking cessation and reduced smoking prevalence.

sections.label: Rotating images and 75% GHWs
sections.summary: Images are rotated to avoid desensitisation, and GHWs are proposed to increase to 75% of cigarette packaging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, you rotate and change the images because, otherwise, one becomes desensitised and dulled to the images.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This recommendation is also in part why we have proposed that the GHWs be increased to 75% of the cigarette packaging.

sections.label: WTO Panel on standardised packaging
sections.summary: The WTO Panel concluded evidence did not show standardised packaging in Australia increased illicit tobacco trade or consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The WTO Panel concluded that the evidence did not demonstrate that the introduction of standardised packaging in Australia had led to an increased trade or consumption of illicit tobacco so as to undermine standardised packaging's contribution to the overall objective of improving public health.

sections.label: Monitoring illicit trade
sections.summary: There is no compelling reason to believe counterfeit products and illicit trade will increase with standardised packaging, but monitoring continues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Overall, therefore, there is no compelling reason to believe that counterfeit products and illicit trade will increase with the introduction of standardised packaging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will, however, work with Customs and other relevant agencies to continue to monitor the situation regarding illicit trade and step up enforcement and educational efforts as necessary.

sections.label: Advance notice for tobacco packaging
sections.summary: Past tobacco packaging changes in Singapore, such as the GHW change, had nine to 12 months' advance notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In Singapore, for past changes to tobacco packaging, for example, the GHW change, we have provided advance notice of somewhere between nine to 12 months' lead time.

sections.label: Tobacco dealing licence requirement
sections.summary: Section 18 requires anyone dealing with tobacco products, including importing, distributing and selling, to hold a valid HSA licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Section 18 is the provision that requires any person dealing with tobacco products – and that includes the importing, distributing, selling and offering for sale in Singapore – to hold a valid licence issued by HSA.

sections.label: Penalties for duty evasion offenders
sections.summary: Offenders face a fine of up to 40 times the duty evaded, up to six years' jail, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Offenders face a fine of up to 40 times the amount of duty evaded, or up to six years' jail or both.

sections.label: Import ban on non-compliant packs
sections.summary: The proposed amendments will not allow importation of any packs not complying with standardised packaging regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If Members look at the proposed amendments, no importation of any packs not in compliance with the standardised packaging regulations will be allowed.

sections.label: Reasons for standardised packaging proposal
sections.summary: Smoking rates have not clearly declined continuously and over 2,000 Singaporeans die prematurely yearly from smoking-related diseases, so the SP Proposal was not taken lightly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Smoking rates in recent years have not shown a clear pattern of continuous decline, and more than 2,000 Singaporeans die prematurely from smoking-related diseases each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The decision to introduce the SP Proposal, that is, to introduce standardised packaging of tobacco products and to enlarge our existing GHW size, was not taken lightly.

sections.label: Expected public health benefits
sections.summary: The SP Proposal is expected to serve positive objectives and provide substantial public health benefits, including reduced smoking prevalence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ultimately, the SP Proposal is expected to serve positive objectives and provide substantial public health benefits, including leading to reduced smoking prevalence in Singapore.
